reason: Copying the existing DNA directly addresses the goal of giving each daughter a complete genome.
expectation: The DNA nucleotides will be used to copy the cell's nuclear DNA, preparing it for division.

alternatives.reason: Building the spindle is also necessary, but copying the genome first seems a natural starting point.

effect: The DNA is copied into sister chromatids; the next goal needs a spindle and a grown cell.
reaction: The old-and-new strand detail makes the copying process clear.
reason: Build the spindle needed to separate the copied chromosomes.
expectation: The proteins and duplicated centrosomes will form a chromosome-moving spindle.

alternatives.reason: New membrane is also needed for growth, but I will build the spindle first.

reason: The only offered combination prepares the membrane needed for cell growth.

effect: The vesicles provide a membrane supply routed through the ER and Golgi; the cell can now grow.
reaction: The delivery pathway makes the membrane-building step easier to follow.
reason: The only offered combination uses the membrane supply to enlarge the cell.
expectation: The vesicles will add membrane to the cell, producing a grown cell with copied DNA.

effect: The cell has grown and retains its copied nuclear DNA, so it is ready for the spindle.
reaction: The completed labels make its readiness clear.
reason: The only offered combination applies the spindle to form daughter nuclei.
expectation: The spindle will separate the sister chromatids and help form two daughter nuclei.

effect: The copied chromosomes have separated into two nuclei, but the cytoplasm remains connected.
reaction: The time-strip clearly distinguishes nuclear division from cytoplasmic division.
reason: The only offered combination uses actin and myosin to divide the cytoplasm.
expectation: Actin and myosin will constrict the cell and separate it into two daughter cells, each with a nucleus.

effect: The cytoplasm has separated into two daughter stem cells, each with a complete genome; the chapter is complete.
reaction: The distinction between continued self-renewal and later differentiation gives the outcome useful context.

mostWorthwhile.text: Applying the spindle was most worthwhile: the planned time-strip connects chromosome separation to two nuclei while making clear that the cytoplasm is still joined.

leastWorthwhile.text: Enlarging the cell was clear but comparatively routine; its result mostly confirmed the two completed prerequisites.

surprise.text: The spindle appeared as a preview of assembly during mitosis, with a caption clarifying its timing after DNA copying. That helped reconcile building it before growing the cell in the game.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, though several later combinations were the only offered action. The spindle picture mentions tubulin without explaining it, which may leave its connection to the general protein item unclear.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the daughter cells differentiate into muscle and lining, although the largely forced sequence left limited room for meaningful choices.
